---
title: "One dataset on Hugging Face and Kaggle"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The rtemis demo dataset is hosted on two sites: as [rtemis/demo](https://huggingface.co/datasets/rtemis/demo) on the Hugging Face Hub and as [rtemisorg/rtemis-demo](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/rtemisorg/rtemis-demo) on Kaggle. Both copies hold the same two Parquet files, `data/regression.parquet` and `data/classification.parquet`, and the same Croissant file, `croissant.json`, which describes them.

Each site also generates its own Croissant metadata for every dataset it hosts. This article reads the metadata each site generates, compares the two documents with the dataset's own `croissant.json`, and reads the records from each site through the dataset's own metadata.

The article downloads from both sites when it is built.

```{r library}
library(croissant)
# One cache per site, so that each site's files download from that site
cache_hf <- tempfile("croissant_hf_")
cache_kaggle <- tempfile("croissant_kaggle_")
```

## The metadata each site generates

`read_croissant_hf()` reads the metadata the Hub generates from its Parquet conversion of the dataset and from the dataset card.

```{r hf-generated}
hf_generated <- read_croissant_hf("rtemis/demo")
hf_generated
```

`read_croissant_kaggle()` reads the metadata Kaggle generates, the document that the dataset page offers as "Export metadata as Croissant".

```{r kaggle-generated}
kaggle_generated <- read_croissant_kaggle("rtemisorg/rtemis-demo")
kaggle_generated
```

## The dataset's own metadata

`croissant.json` is an ordinary file of each copy of the dataset; neither site reads it or changes it. `read_croissant()` reads it from the Hub by its `hf://datasets/` path, here at the tag `v1.0.0`, and `read_croissant_kaggle()` reads it from Kaggle when given its path in the dataset as `file`.

```{r own}
own_hf <- read_croissant("hf://datasets/rtemis/demo@v1.0.0/croissant.json")
own_kaggle <- read_croissant_kaggle("rtemisorg/rtemis-demo", file = "croissant.json")
own_hf
```

The two objects differ only in `base`, the location each document's relative `contentUrl`s resolve against: the Hub revision for one and the Kaggle API for the other.

```{r base}
own_hf@base
own_kaggle@base
```

`write_croissant()` writes the metadata without `base`, and writes the same JSON-LD for both.

```{r identical-metadata}
identical(write_croissant(own_hf), write_croissant(own_kaggle))
```

## Comparison

The following table summarizes each document with the accessors `about()`, `files()`, `record_sets()`, `enumerations()`, and `fields()`.

```{r summarize}
summarize_croissant <- function(x) {
  a <- about(x)
  or_absent <- function(v) {
    if (is.null(v)) "absent" else paste(v, collapse = ", ")
  }
  rs <- names(record_sets(x))
  f <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(rs, function(r) fields(x, r)))
  n_described <- if (nrow(f) > 0L) sum(!is.na(f[["description"]])) else 0L
  c(
    `Croissant version` = x@version,
    `Dataset version` = or_absent(a[["dataset_version"]]),
    License = or_absent(a[["license"]]),
    Creator = or_absent(a[["creator"]]),
    `citeAs` = if (is.null(a[["cite_as"]])) "absent" else "present",
    `datePublished` = or_absent(a[["date_published"]]),
    Files = paste(
      paste0(files(x)[["id"]], " (", files(x)[["encoding_format"]], ")"),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    `Record sets` = if (length(rs) > 0L) paste(rs, collapse = ", ") else "none",
    Enumerations = as.character(length(enumerations(x))),
    `Fields with a description` = paste0(n_described, " of ", nrow(f)),
    `Data types` = if (nrow(f) > 0L) {
      paste(sort(unique(f[["data_type"]])), collapse = ", ")
    } else {
      "none"
    }
  )
}
comparison <- data.frame(
  `Hugging Face generated` = summarize_croissant(hf_generated),
  `Kaggle generated` = summarize_croissant(kaggle_generated),
  `croissant.json, either site` = summarize_croissant(own_hf),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(comparison)
```

The Hub describes its Parquet conversion of the data, stored on the branch `refs/convert/parquet`: one file set and one record set per table, with an added `split` field whose values an enumeration lists. Its data types come from the Parquet schema, and its `name`, `description`, `license`, and `keywords` from the dataset card.

Kaggle describes the version's zip archive and the files within it whose format it recognizes; its `name`, `alternateName`, `description`, `license`, and `keywords` come from the dataset's settings on Kaggle.

The dataset's own metadata names each Parquet file with its SHA-256, gives each field a description and the data type of its R column, and lists the levels of each categorical field in an enumeration.

## Validation

`validate_croissant()` reports the issues of each document.

```{r validate}
validate_croissant(hf_generated)
validate_croissant(kaggle_generated)
validate_croissant(own_hf)
```

## Records

`read_record_set()` reads a record set from the files its metadata names. The Hub-generated record set `classification` reads from the Hub's Parquet conversion:

```{r records-hf-generated}
generated <- read_record_set(
  hf_generated,
  "classification",
  cache_dir = cache_hf
)
dim(generated)
```

The dataset's own record set `classification` reads from the uploaded Parquet file, from each site. Each download is verified: from the Hub against the SHA-256 the Hub lists for the file, and from Kaggle against the SHA-256 in the metadata.

```{r records-own}
from_hf <- read_record_set(own_hf, "classification", cache_dir = cache_hf)
from_kaggle <- read_record_set(
  own_kaggle,
  "classification",
  cache_dir = cache_kaggle
)
identical(from_hf, from_kaggle)
dim(from_hf)
```

The Hub-generated records hold the `split` column in addition to the dataset's columns:

```{r records-columns}
setdiff(names(generated), names(from_hf))
```

The dataset's own metadata describes each column, as `fields()` returns:

```{r fields}
knitr::kable(fields(own_hf, "classification")[c(1L, 101L), c("column", "description")])
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(c(cache_hf, cache_kaggle), recursive = TRUE)
```
